Moon Druid/Barbarian

  • Method: Take one level in Barbarian
  • Reason: 1) Good chunk of health of additional health (1d12), 2) More AC from the Barbarians Unarmored Defense (Add Con mod to AC), 3) Rage while in beast form since you can't cast spells anyways and gain resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, & Slashing, and 4) If you're a Brown Bear, then you're also doing a pretty decent amount of damage [1d8 + 2d6 + 8] (Average Result = 11.5+8 = 19.5)2 (Add +2 for when raging). The +10 is from the Brown Bear's Str mod (+4) times 2 and then adding the Rage damage.
  • Notes: Sacrificing unlimited Wild Shapes at level 20. It's arguably the best capstone.

Polearm Champion Fighter (PCF)4

  • Method: 1) Race: Half-Orc, 2) Archetype: Champion Fighter, 3) Weapon: Glaive/Halberd/Pike, and 4) Feat: Polearm Master
  • Reason: 1) At level 4, this allows you do 2 attacks in one turn and do the bonus action to hit with the butt of the glaive.   • Notes: 1) Grab the Charger feat at level 65 for additional +5 damage. 2) If your DM rules that Polearm Master lets you use an Opportunity Attack when you approach a creature since it's entering your reach, then this build could theoretically allow you do [9d10 + 3d4 + (Str mod * 4)] in one turn, by going Move > Reaction > Attack > Bonus Action > Action Surge. 3) If #2 is allowed, then it would be worth looking into getting Mobile over Charger since you'd rarely provoke Opportunity Attacks and could just run back-and-forth across the field wrecking enemies. 4) I don't think I'd allow #2 since enemies don't provoke when you leave. What Are Your Favorite Optimized Early-Game Builds?

Several notes:

Warlock: Get the Pact of the Chain to get a familiar, get the power to see through their eyes, and I'm pretty sure one of the familiars can turn invisible. Now you can ignore cover while using your familiar to spot your enemies to snipe them from 600 feet away. Alternatively, get the power to cast Arcane Eye at 15 for free for the same effect, since it has unlimited movement range.

Bearbarian: Make sure it's a gnome. Gnomes get advantage on all intellectual saving throws. This means your bear is now resistant to all physical attacks and has advantage on all saving throws except Constitution (high for a bear anyway, and gets proficiency from Barbarian) and Dexterity (fireballs, whoop-dee-doo). You're now indestructible. I made a character this way. His name was Bear, a gnome raised by bears, wrestled bears, wore the skin of a brother bear who died in a fight as a way to honor his brother. Bear was the shit, and became a professional gladiator/wrestler.

Polearm Champion Fighter: I used a similar build, abuses Attacks of Opportunity, uses the newest Unearthed Arcana for amusing effect.

Black Knight: Human (with the feat variant), level 4 Avenger Paladin, with the Tunnel Fighter fighting style. Pack on both Sentinel and Polearm Master. Not a necessity, but Heavy Armor Master does help, since they'll have to go through YOU first. The fear aura and movement on AoO makes this class ABSOLUTELY TERRIFYING. YOU SHALL NOT PASS.

For the Charger, consider the Minotaur for a feat-less alternative. For a similarly mobile/melee character, here's another variant:

Thumper (Rabbit dasher): Shifter (Longstride), level 4 monk. Pick up the Mobile feat. Shifting grants you temporary hit points and being able to dash as a bonus action for 1 minute (10 rounds).

This means you can move 100 feet (50 speed * 2), and every attempted attack (failed counts) removes the enemies' chance to attack you with an opportunity attack. Considering most enemies don't have 35 speed or more, this means that you can stand 35 feet away, have them move, move 5 feet to hit them, then move 35 feet back (for a total of 40 speed, and you still have 10 left over without dashing). If they refuse to move, you just dash as a bonus action (free while shifting) to get the speed you need to reach them.

As a bonus, you reduce incoming ranged attacks by 1d10 + Dex mod (which you get +2 of from your race) + your monk level. That's an average of 12.5 damage with a Dex mod of 4. You're basically immortal as long as you don't have to roll any saving throws and you have enough space to run in.

Alternatively:

Blur Blade: Either Human level 3, or any race at level 4, Eldritch Knight with the Mobile feat, grabbing Expeditious Retreat for a level 1 spell, and Longstrider if you absolutely need the same strategy as Thumper. The heavy armor and spellcasting gives more versatility to the Blur Blade than the Thumper Monk, but must make constitution saving throws to keep Expeditious Retreat, making it susceptible to ranged harassment.

With the Swashbuckler Rogue getting the ability to naturally deny Attacks of Opportunity, it would do well with a race with naturally high speed, like the Forest Elf, or even better, the Arrakocra (with its flying speed of 50, Dex bonus, and limitations of armor). It would play very similarly to this type of gameplay of hit-and-run melee.

One that a friend suggested was the:

Ward Warrior: 3 Eldritch Knight, 2 Abjuration Wizard, any race (although Earth Genasi get Pass Without Trace for free, which is an abjuration spell.)

Use your reactions to cast spells like Shield and Absorb Elements (activating your Abjuration Ward) as you go to town on the enemy. Lacks much damage, but you'll never die. Keep in mind, since two handed weapons only need to be held with two hands when you are swinging, you don't need the War Caster feat to cast spells with a two handed weapon when it's not on your turn. You WILL need War Caster if you decide to go sword and shield, though.
